headline: Volumes fall, net loss deepens on notable items
summary_short: Mosaic's Q2 2026 revenue fell 6.0% y/y to $2,824M and the company swung to a $273M net loss (-$0.86 diluted EPS) from $411M of net income a year ago, hurt by lower volumes, higher raw material costs, and $351M of pretax notable items; adjusted EBITDA fell to $407M from $566M.
summary_long: Revenue fell 6.0% y/y to $2,824M as lower Potash and Fertilizantes volumes and Phosphate curtailments outweighed higher DAP/MOP prices. Operating income swung to a $36M loss from $244M of earnings, though the loss narrowed sharply from Q1's $373M level, which included a $422M Fertilizantes impairment tied to the Brazil asset review. Net loss was $273M ($0.86 diluted loss/share) after $351M of pretax notable items — mainly a $162M Ma'aden mark-to-market charge, a $69M write-off, and $49M of FX losses; adjusted EPS was $0.13. Cash was $294M; free cash flow was $(153)M on capex timing. Mosaic cut 2026 capex guidance to $1.2B from $1.25B and settled Q3 sulfur contracts at $705/long ton.

drivers.explanation: Potash net sales fell to $650M from $711M on lower volumes (2.0 vs 2.3Mt) despite a higher MOP price ($275 vs $261/t); Fertilizantes fell to $1,034M from $1,175M on lower volumes (1.5 vs 2.2Mt); Phosphate rose to $1,246M from $1,173M on a higher DAP price.

Notable items cut EPS by $0.99/sh this quarter (mainly a $0.43/sh Ma'aden mark-to-market charge, $0.17/sh asset write-off, $0.10/sh FX loss and $0.10/sh tax item), versus a $0.78/sh positive notable-items swing a year ago.
Results primarily reflected lower sales volumes and higher raw material costs in Phosphate and Mosaic Fertilizantes, which were partially offset by higher phosphate and potash prices.
Phosphate gross margin swung to $(4)/tonne from $67/tonne a year ago as blended rock cost ($90 vs $74/t) and cash cost of conversion ($129 vs $126/t) rose faster than the DAP price gain.

The $337M q/q narrowing of the operating loss mainly reflects the absence of Q1's $422M Mosaic Fertilizantes operating loss, partly offset by a wider Phosphate operating loss this quarter ($104M vs $48M in Q1).

Swung to a $36M loss from $244M of earnings as Phosphate fell to a $104M loss (from an $8M loss) and Fertilizantes swung to a $41M loss (from $109M of earnings); Potash was roughly flat ($195M vs $194M).

Widened mainly on the operating-income swing above plus $351M of pretax notable items (Ma'aden mark-to-market, write-offs, FX losses), versus a $339M net positive notable-items swing in the year-ago quarter.
Tracks the pretax-loss widening above; the effective tax rate was 11.2% (4.5% adjusted for notable items) in the quarter.
Not detailed in the release; cash flow shows $167M of operating cash flow and $320M of capex ($(153)M free cash flow), plus a $1B term loan issued to refinance short-term commercial paper.
Essentially unchanged y/y (317.9M vs 319.0M); not explained in the release.

Tracks the operating/pretax-income swing described above; this Yahoo-sourced GAAP figure nets non-operating items differently than the release's own operating-loss line and is not itself a company-disclosed figure.

This Yahoo-sourced GAAP figure is far below the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of $407M because it does not add back the $351M of pretax notable items that the company's own reconciliation excludes.

CEO Bruce Bodine cited "sulfur availability and affordability challenges," saying Mosaic cut phosphate production and capex, completed the Carlsbad mine sale, and lowered 2026 capex guidance to preserve financial flexibility.
